text: Shell.jsx's <main> padding: var(--eb-space-6) is the single source of the page gutter on ALL FOUR sides (not just horizontal); PatternsCatalog.jsx, SdlcCatalogPage.jsx, and MainframeCatalogPage.jsx each additionally set their own page-level padding (var(--eb-space-8)/var(--eb-space-6)) on their outer wrapper, doubling the inset — same bug class as KnowledgeFlow.jsx's redundant space-4 padding (#533), fixed together in PR #535.
summary: Shell.jsx already adds spacing around all four sides of every page, but three catalog pages were mistakenly adding their own extra spacing on top of that, causing double the intended gap. This was the same kind of duplicate-padding bug found earlier in KnowledgeFlow.jsx, and all four were fixed together in PR 535.

text: KB storage branch (env.knowledgeStore.repoRef.branch, resolved by resolveKnowledgeBranch in orchestrator/knowledge-sync.js) is a SEPARATE concept from a repository's code branch; normalizeKnowledgeStore's in-repo fallback must adopt only a repo's url+credentials (adoptRepoForKnowledge), never its code branch, or an unconfigured team silently pushes knowledge to the code branch. Default KB branch is 'agent-knowledge' (not protected).
summary: The branch used to store team knowledge is always its own separate branch, never the same branch used for coding work. If a team has not set one up, the system should only borrow the repository address and login details, not the code branch, otherwise knowledge files could accidentally end up mixed in with code; the default knowledge branch is called agent-knowledge.

text: Knowledge-learning settings (autonomy/review/promotion-gates) are rendered by ONE shared React component admin-console/src/components/KnowledgeLearningConfig.jsx (default export KnowledgeLearningSections; exports AUTONOMY_LEVELS/GATE_ORDER/GATE_LABELS/GATE_TIPS/KNOWLEDGE_LEARNING_DEFAULTS/PanelSection), consumed by BOTH the Knowledge-page slide-out panel (KnowledgeFlow.jsx, PUTs live) and the Team-Setup wizard Knowledge step (TeamSetup.jsx, mutates form state; readOnly in extend mode). Storage config is intentionally NOT in this component (KnowledgeFlow-only). Added in PR #579 (#567); don't reintroduce a divergent second copy of the copy/controls.
summary: The settings for how knowledge learning works (like autonomy levels and promotion gates) all live in one shared component that is reused in both the Knowledge page panel and the Team-Setup wizard, so if you need to change that UI or its logic, do it there and do not create a separate duplicate copy.

text: Role templates are a two-tier store (#587/PR#591): repo-seeded defaults in AGENT_TEMPLATES_DIR (wiped by make seed-templates) are overlaid by a durable user store USER_AGENT_TEMPLATES_DIR=/workspace/agent-templates; admin-console read loaders listAgentTemplateIds/loadAgentTemplate are overlay-aware (user file shadows default), so UI create/edit/delete of role templates survives a re-seed and is picked up by wizard/Flow picker without redeploy.
summary: Role templates are stored in two layers: a default set that can be reset by reseeding, and a separate user-editable store that sits on top and takes priority. Any templates you create or edit through the admin console are saved in the user layer, so they survive a reseed and show up in the wizard without needing a redeploy.

text: gh pr edit --remove-label can silently no-op on the first call (label reappears on next view); always re-verify labels with gh pr view --json labels after editing and re-remove if the label persists.
summary: Removing a label from a pull request using the command line can sometimes appear to work but silently fail, leaving the label still attached. Always double-check the labels after making the change and remove the label again if it has come back.

text: GET /api/auth/session (admin-console/api/auth.js ~192-196) returns only {authenticated, user:{username}} — NO role/scope/systemAdmin flag; so AuthContext.jsx (user={username}) and Shell.jsx (static NAV array, no role filter) can't hide admin-only nav/pages for non-System-Admins. Exposing caller role+memberships here is the frontend prerequisite for team-visibility gating (issue #584).
summary: The login session response only tells the app whether a user is signed in and what their username is, but leaves out their role or permissions, so the app has no way to show or hide admin-only sections based on who is actually logged in. Adding role and membership info to that response is the required first step before the team can control which parts of the interface different users are allowed to see.

text: In the knowledge CLI (agent-image/scripts/knowledge), _git() prepends `git -C <checkout>`, so a caller can inject inline `-c user.name=...`/`-c user.email=...` via its args to set committer identity per-commit (valid `git -C <root> -c ... commit`), mirroring gh-as-agent commit — committer email is agent-<id>@ace.local while the author marker stays <id>@agents.local for poller loop-protection.
summary: The knowledge CLI sets up Git commits so that each commit is stamped with two different email addresses on purpose: one identifies the agent as the committer, and a slightly different one marks it as the author, which lets the system tell the difference between its own commits and external ones to avoid processing them in a loop.

text: The composed CLAUDE.md Skills section (prompt-assembly.js skillsSection) now injects each granted skill's SKILL.md `description` (name + one-line desc), resolved via resolveSkillSourceDir (agent→team→global, same tier as seeding); assembleClaudeMd stays pure by taking a caller-supplied skillDescriptions map read in buildAgentClaudeMd (orchestrator.js).
summary: When building an agent's instruction file, the system now automatically looks up and includes a short description for each skill the agent has been granted, pulling that info from the skill's own definition file. The lookup follows the same priority order used elsewhere, and the assembly step itself stays simple by receiving the descriptions pre-loaded from outside.

text: prompt-assembly.js interactionNote() preamble contains em-dashes (' — '), so a test asserting 'no ` — ` separator' must scope to the relevant section (e.g. md.split('## Skills')[1]), not the whole composed CLAUDE.md.
summary: When checking that a certain separator character does not appear in a specific section of the document, make sure your test only looks at that section rather than the whole file, since the separator already appears elsewhere in the preamble text.

text: KnowledgeFlow.jsx PromotionDialog keys its copy off `aggregated = !suggestion.id (manual) || suggestion.source==='related'`; a SINGLE manual lesson still has aggregated===true, so combine-phrasing reads wrong — gate singular copy on `single = aggregated && (suggestion.lessonCount||memberTexts.length) <= 1`. manualSuggestionFrom(list) sets lessonCount=list.length and entryIds for any length>=1.
summary: When a user manually submits just one lesson, the dialog incorrectly shows wording meant for combining multiple lessons, because the code treats any manual entry as "aggregated" regardless of count. The fix is to add an extra check so that single-item cases get the correct singular phrasing instead.

text: Promoting a knowledge lesson to a skill accepts an entryIds array of length 1 end-to-end: admin-console/api/knowledge-suggestions.js validatePromotion requires entryIds.length>=1 (not >=2) and api.js adHocCandidate dedups any length — no >=2 guard on the backend.
summary: When promoting a knowledge lesson to a skill, you only need to supply a single entry in the list, not two or more. The system checks for at least one entry and handles any duplicates automatically, so there is no hidden two-entry minimum anywhere in the process.

text: KnowledgeFlow.jsx: the Skills column nodes are graph.nodes.filter(kind==='skill') from buildKnowledgeGraph (knowledge-graph.js), which since #620/PR#623 dedupes skill records to ONE node per name (team-owned card wins, unions provenance entry-ids, sets node.alsoGlobal when a promoted-to-global copy coexists). PromotionDialog now takes a teamSkills prop = those same nodes as the single 'this team's skills' source for its team-tier extend dropdown; effective extend scope is derived from the selected target (global-pool file -> to:'global' via the team->global transition), not the tier chip.
summary: Each skill in the team view now appears just once no matter how many sources it comes from, with the team's own version taking priority, and the dialog for promoting skills to a wider pool pulls from that same deduplicated list to determine what can be extended.

text: KnowledgeFlow.jsx PromotionDialog eligible extend targets for tier==='team' now derive from teamSkills (graph skill nodes) rather than skills.filter(source==='team'), so adopted/promoted global skills visible in the column are selectable; effectiveTo is derived from selectedTarget.scope (not the tier chip) to send the correct to:'global' scope to the backend.
summary: When promoting a skill to the team tier, the list of valid targets now comes from the skill graph rather than a simpler filtered list, so globally adopted skills that appear in the column are included as options. The destination scope sent to the backend is also now taken from the selected target itself, ensuring the correct scope is used instead of relying on the tier label.

text: skill.json (content lineage: version/contentHash/history/origin) is a NEW sidecar distinct from provenance.json (knowledge lineage); the pure core orchestrator/skill-manifest.js is byte-identical-mirrored in admin-console/api/skill-manifest.js with a shared golden fixture (orchestrator/skill-manifest.fixture.json) + a two-sided guard test, same discipline as knowledge-digest.js (added #625/PR#636).
summary: A new file called skill.json was introduced to track the version history of skills, and it is separate from the existing provenance.json which tracks knowledge history. To keep both sides of the system in sync, the core skill-manifest logic is kept identical in two places and protected by a shared test fixture that catches any drift between them.

text: Startup backfill for skill.json lives in admin-console (app.listen callback) only — orchestrator mounts /template-workspace read-only and cannot write to the global pool. Agent-tier skills are stamped lazily on first GET /api/skills or GET /api/skills/:name/content read.
summary: When the system starts up, the admin console is the only place that fills in the initial skills list, while the orchestrator can only read templates and cannot add to that list itself. Individual agent skills only get set up the first time someone actually requests them.

text: persistKnowledgeSummaries (#635) calls the full runConvergenceCollector (not a lighter write path), mirroring archiveKnowledgeEntry — this means a summary backfill can trigger auto-promotion side effects at autonomy >= 3, which is intentional but surprising if not expected.
summary: When saving knowledge summaries, the system runs the same full process used for archiving knowledge entries, which means filling in old summaries can unexpectedly trigger automatic promotions if a certain autonomy level is reached — this is by design, but can catch you off guard if you are not aware of it.

text: Unified skill tier-transfer (#626/PR#638): ONE pure planner admin-console/api/skill-transfer.js (planTransfer/permitTransfer/requiredPermission/transferAction/resolveCollisionName/buildTransferOrigin) + ONE endpoint POST /api/skills/transfer replace scattered promote/lift/share. COPY_ACTION matrix: agent>team=lifted, team>team=shared, team>global=promoted, global>team=adopted; move stamps 'moved' but keeps semanticAction. /api/skills/promote (agent>global cell retired) + /api/skills/promote-to-global are now deprecated comment-only wrappers, dropped from UI.
summary: All the old separate skill-promotion and sharing endpoints were replaced by a single transfer endpoint that handles every combination of moving a skill between agents, teams, and global, automatically labeling the result based on where it came from and where it went. The older promote endpoints still exist in the code for now but are no longer used in the interface.

text: /api/knowledge/share-to-team (ShareDialog, team→team) only copies SKILL.md — not the full skill directory — unlike POST /api/skills/transfer which does a full cpSync; migrating ShareDialog to the engine unifies this behavior.
summary: When sharing a skill between teams through the share dialog, only a single file gets copied over, not the entire skill folder like a full transfer would do. Moving the share dialog to use the same underlying system as full transfers will fix this inconsistency.

text: For skill/KB flows in 314092, 'route the ShareDialog/lift path through the engine' (issue #626 §3) means BACKEND delegation — /api/knowledge/promote & share-to-team keep their KB work (LLM-re-synthesised SKILL.md, entryIds, convergence, candidate lifecycle, extend mode, #559 cleanup) and call the engine for the file write; it does NOT mean pointing the frontend at POST /api/skills/transfer, which does only a verbatim cpSync + origin-only stamp and would drop all that KB lineage/content.
summary: When sharing or promoting knowledge base content, the backend handles all the important work like restructuring content and tracking history, and only asks the engine to handle the actual file writing. Using the simpler transfer endpoint instead would skip all that work and lose the knowledge base history, so it should not be used for this purpose.

text: gh-as-agent commit does NOT stage files (no implicit -a) — run git add <file> first or the commit reports 'no changes added to commit'.
summary: When using the commit action in gh-as-agent, files are not automatically included in the commit, so you must manually stage them with git add first. Skipping that step will result in a message saying there is nothing to commit.

text: Override-stranding fix (#627): orchestrator setTeamSkillActive on a DEACTIVATE calls planSkillSync with includeMembers:[] so override members get skip-override (files+config kept) — that strands the skill once the pool dir is deleted. The fix strips the name from each opted-in (includeMembers) member's own skillsOverride and removes its files, AFTER the main results loop, guarded against double-sync.
summary: When deactivating a skill for the whole team, members who had personally opted in were being left with broken leftovers because the system skipped cleaning up their individual overrides. The fix adds a cleanup step after the main process that properly removes those personal overrides and their files for each affected member.

text: Knowledge live-feed (api.js): kbParseLine parses ANY JSON object (no event-type whitelist) and knowledgeLinks.matchesScope filters purely by event.teamId (team:<id> scope) / event.agentId (agent:<id> scope), global/'' sees all. So any new appendSkillFeedEvent-style event (skill-deleted/skill-restored/skill-transfer/activation) flows to the SSE stream with NO frontend change — but it MUST carry teamId (team tier) / agentId (agent tier) or the scope filter silently drops it for non-global subscribers.
summary: Any new event type you add will automatically appear in the live knowledge feed without touching the frontend, as long as the event includes the right team or agent ID so the system knows who should see it. If that ID is missing, the event gets silently ignored for everyone except global subscribers.

text: GitHub Event Log session correlationId contract is trigger:<triggerId>:gh:<eventId> (stamped by agent-entrypoint.py _execute_inner). To match a session: active sessions carry a single correlationId; finished sessions carry a correlationIds[] SET (grouped by Claude session-id since #555). Match active first, else history, else show a non-blocking not-found banner (never a blank view).
summary: When GitHub events come in, each one gets a special ID that links it to a session, and the system checks active sessions first, then past ones, to find the right match. If nothing is found, it shows a small notice instead of leaving the screen blank.

text: admin-console/api tests can't run the full 'node --test' suite in the sandbox: auth.test.js fails with MODULE_NOT_FOUND for express-rate-limit (auth.js:18) because there is no node_modules. This is a pre-existing environmental failure — verify a new suite by running only the dep-free test files touched, not the whole directory.
summary: Running the full API test suite in the sandbox will always break because a required package is missing from the environment, and this is a known existing issue. When verifying new tests, only run the specific files you changed rather than the whole test directory.

text: The repo now has CI: .github/workflows/ci.yml (added via PR #670 for #665) runs four jobs on every pull_request and push to main — orchestrator (node --test), admin-console/api (node --test), admin-console (vite build), agent-image (pytest, py3.12); all green.
summary: Every pull request and push to the main branch now automatically runs a set of checks across four parts of the codebase to make sure nothing is broken, and all checks are currently passing.

text: A GitHub workflow with `on: workflow_dispatch` can only be manually triggered if the workflow file exists on the repo's DEFAULT branch — `gh workflow run <wf> --ref <feature-branch>` returns 'HTTP 404: workflow not found on the default branch' when the workflow lives only on the feature branch, so pre-merge burn-in of a not-yet-merged CI workflow requires landing it on main first (or the first post-merge nightly).
summary: To manually trigger a GitHub workflow, the workflow file must already exist on the main branch, not just on a feature branch. This means you cannot fully test a brand-new CI workflow before merging it into main.

text: The admin-console backend POST /api/llm-endpoints already accepts authType / complianceAck / oauthFlowId — adding oauth-token (Claude subscription/Enterprise) Model Provider support to a UI flow needs NO backend provider-creation change. For oauth providers a pasted authToken WINS over a completed oauthFlowId login flow (drop the flow id when a token is pasted); creating an oauth provider requires an explicit single-user complianceAck.
summary: The backend already supports everything needed for oauth-based AI model providers, so only UI changes are required. When setting one up, a manually pasted auth token takes priority over a completed login flow, and the person creating it must explicitly confirm a compliance acknowledgment.

text: work-items.js workItemDetail() returns 'runs' as the run-ROWS array (overriding renderWorkItem's numeric runs count) — callers wanting the count must use detail.runs.length, not detail.runs
summary: When you ask for details about a work item, the runs field gives you a list of individual run records, not a simple number. So if you need to know how many runs there are, you have to check the length of that list yourself.

text: admin-console/api/auth.test.js fails in the agent sandbox with 'Cannot find module express-rate-limit' — a pre-existing missing-dependency issue (node_modules not fully installed), unrelated to code changes; the rest of node --test admin-console/api/*.test.js passes.
summary: One test file fails in the sandbox simply because a required package was never fully installed there, not because of anything wrong with the code itself. All the other tests in that same group run and pass fine.

text: candidateFromEntries in knowledge-suggestions.js originally dropped each entry's `kind` when building members[]; carry it through if a downstream consumer (e.g. heuristic draft grouping) needs per-statement kind.
summary: When building a list of suggested knowledge entries, the code used to lose track of what type each entry was. If anything later in the process needs to know each entry's type, make sure that information is kept and passed along.

text: In admin-console/src/pages/agent-chat/WorkspaceBrowser.jsx the tree indent step is 12px/level (paddingLeft `16 + depth*12`); folder rows (DirNode) lead with a Caret(11px)+2px-gap chevron gutter before the folder icon, so leaf/file rows (Row) must reserve that same 11px+2px gutter to align file icons with sibling folder icons.
summary: In the file browser tree, each level of nesting adds 12px of indentation, and folder rows include a small arrow icon that takes up 13px of space before the folder icon. File rows that have no arrow must still leave that same 13px gap so their icons line up neatly with sibling folder icons.
